headline: scRNA-seq reference choice shapes spatial deconvolution in breast cancer
label: Benchmarking Computational Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Recent benchmarks and tools expose how reference choice and sample design condition single-cell and spatial inference outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how reference data and input design condition computational inference from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. The only explicit benchmark here evaluates scRNA-seq reference selection for Cell2location and RCTD deconvolution of breast cancer Xenium and MERFISH spatial datasets, showing that reference choice affects deconvolution outcomes. Other items engage the same dependence by design: Cavebear transfers pseudotime structure from reference time-series to query species or conditions, and SIMPlex generates matched spatial and single-nucleus profiles from one section to avoid reliance on public reference single-cell data. LucaCell replaces gene IDs with mRNA sequence embeddings for cross-species annotation. The remaining preprints and papers, including CellART, scFLAME, and spAlignDE, develop methods without comparative benchmarking. What is new is explicit benchmarking of reference dependence alongside tools that aim to reduce it.
